# Kinetis

> A PHP framework for persistent-worker runtimes such as FrankenPHP and
> RoadRunner, which also run unchanged under PHP-FPM and AWS Lambda.
> Attribute-driven routing, validation and OpenAPI; a two-tier
> request-scoped container; Fiber-based concurrency over Revolt; a native
> Model Context Protocol server.

Kinetis core ships as `kinetis/framework`, requiring PHP 8.4 or later.
Optional capabilities ship as separate packages. Reference pages hold
exact contracts and internal workings behind the guides.

The pages are ordered the way an application is built: start with the
tutorial, then read whichever section you have reached.

## Start here

- [Tutorial](https://kinetis.dev/docs/tutorial.html): Build a real-time application from scratch: a database, a queue, a scheduled command, and live updates over a WebSocket.
- [Core Concepts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/core-concepts.html): The runtime-agnostic Kernel, the request lifecycle, and why persistent workers change the rules.

## Building an application

- [Configuration](https://kinetis.dev/docs/config.html): Set environment keys and inject typed Config values.
- [Bootstrapping](https://kinetis.dev/docs/bootstrapping.html): Register application services and global middleware before the container locks.
- [Routing & Validation](https://kinetis.dev/docs/routing-validation.html): Attribute-based routes, typed DTOs, constraint validation, and zero-config OpenAPI.
- [Middleware](https://kinetis.dev/docs/middleware.html): The PSR-15 middleware pipeline: global vs. route, plus the built-in ExceptionHandlerMiddleware/CorsMiddleware/RateLimitMiddleware.
- [Events](https://kinetis.dev/docs/events.html): A PSR-14 event dispatcher with attribute-driven listener registration, plus ShouldQueue for deferring a listener to a queue.
- [CLI](https://kinetis.dev/docs/cli.html): The kinetis CLI: built-in commands, application commands via #[Command], commands from installed packages, and restricting discovery.
- [Testing](https://kinetis.dev/docs/testing.html): TestClient, for exercising a Kernel end-to-end in a consumer's own test suite.
- [Views](https://kinetis.dev/docs/views.html): One controller-facing view API with mutually exclusive pure PHP, Latte, and Twig adapters, plus the asset() helper.

## Working with data

- [Database](https://kinetis.dev/docs/persistence.html): Install kinetis/database-bridge, configure MySQL or PostgreSQL, inject a link and run transactions.
- [Query Builder](https://kinetis.dev/docs/query-builder.html): kinetis/query-builder: a thin, parameterized SQL query builder — not an ORM.
- [ORM](https://kinetis.dev/docs/orm.html): kinetis/orm: a data mapper over the query builder — attributed entities, typed repositories, and a unit of work with an identity map, change tracking and a transactional flush, wired into Kinetis by kinetis/database-bridge.
- [Migrations](https://kinetis.dev/docs/migrations.html): kinetis/migrations: a thin database migration runner — raw SQL up()/down(), no schema-diffing, with the migrate commands on vendor/bin/kinetis.

## Background work

- [Queue](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue.html): Choose a backend, write and push a job, run workers and handle duplicate delivery.
- [Queue (Redis)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-redis.html): Run a single-node Redis queue over kinetis/redis; Redis Cluster is available for application cache use.
- [Queue (SQL)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-sql.html): kinetis/queue-sql: a MySQL/Postgres backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.
- [Queue (SQS)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-sqs.html): kinetis/queue-sqs: an Amazon SQS backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.
- [Queue (RabbitMQ)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-rabbitmq.html): kinetis/queue-rabbitmq: a RabbitMQ backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.

## Authentication and sessions

- [Authentication](https://kinetis.dev/docs/auth.html): kinetis/auth: opaque Bearer-token authentication middleware.
- [JWT Authentication](https://kinetis.dev/docs/auth-jwt.html): kinetis/auth-jwt: stateless JWT authentication (HS256/RS256), with optional per-token revocation.
- [Sessions & CSRF](https://kinetis.dev/docs/session.html): Choose a session store, pass a CSRF token to a view and submit it through a form or request header.
- [Authorization](https://kinetis.dev/docs/authorization.html): kinetis/authorization: ability-based authorization — Gate wraps any callable Policy check, with no attribute, registry, or type-based dispatch.

## Runtime and performance

- [Runtime Adapters](https://kinetis.dev/docs/runtime-adapters.html): FrankenPHP, PHP-FPM, RoadRunner, and AWS Lambda adapters, and how RuntimeDetector picks one.
- [Concurrency](https://kinetis.dev/docs/concurrency.html): Fiber-based concurrency over Revolt: concurrently(), Async\Socket, and Async\Timer.
- [Caching & AOT Compilation](https://kinetis.dev/docs/caching.html): Production-only AOT caching of routes, commands, event listeners, and validation plans, plus APP_ENV.
- [Performance tuning](https://kinetis.dev/docs/performance-tuning.html): Capacity tuning: the worker-threads x maxConnections budget, what to observe under load, and tuning by workload shape.
- [Benchmarks](https://kinetis.dev/docs/benchmarks.html): TechEmpower-style benchmark results against eight other PHP frameworks on isolated AWS hardware, plus a separate FrankenPHP-vs-RoadRunner and Kinetis-vs-Spiral comparison.

## Observability

- [Logging](https://kinetis.dev/docs/logging.html): PSR-3 logging: the default NullLogger, and where Kinetis logs on its own.
- [Telemetry](https://kinetis.dev/docs/telemetry.html): kinetis/telemetry: OpenTelemetry tracing — request spans, SQL/queue decorators, a traced HTTP transport, OTLP export over the Revolt-backed client.

## Integrations

- [Storage](https://kinetis.dev/docs/storage.html): Configure file storage, write and read files, validate uploads and choose local disk or S3.
- [Storage (S3)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/storage-s3.html): Configure an S3 bucket, credentials, visibility and permissions.
- [Mailer](https://kinetis.dev/docs/mailer.html): kinetis/mailer: mail sending via Symfony\Component\Mailer, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client for API-based transports.
- [Broadcasting](https://kinetis.dev/docs/broadcasting.html): kinetis/broadcasting: real-time broadcasting over the Pusher Channels protocol, with private/presence channel authorization.
- [HTTP Client](https://kinetis.dev/docs/revolt-http-client.html): kinetis/revolt-http-client: a Revolt-native Symfony HttpClientInterface — usable standalone, no Kinetis required.
- [Redis](https://kinetis.dev/docs/redis.html): Configure a PSR-16 cache over Redis, TLS and Redis Cluster in a Kinetis application.
- [Search engines](https://kinetis.dev/docs/search-engines.html): Install OpenSearch or Elasticsearch, configure a connection, index documents and search them.
- [Search (OpenSearch)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/search-opensearch.html): kinetis/search-opensearch: OpenSearch client construction, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client.
- [Search (Elasticsearch)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/search-elasticsearch.html): Configure the Elasticsearch client, client major version and API-key authentication.
- [AWS request signing (SigV4)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/aws-sigv4.html): kinetis/aws-sigv4: a PSR-18 client signing requests with AWS Signature Version 4 for one configured origin, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client — usable standalone.

## AI agents

- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/mcp.html): kinetis/mcp: the native Model Context Protocol server — tools, resources, stdio and HTTP transports, on MCP 2025-06-18.
- [MCP Documentation Server](https://kinetis.dev/docs/mcp-docs.html): kinetis/mcp-docs: a standalone, framework-agnostic MCP server serving these pages as resources.
- [Orbitron](https://kinetis.dev/docs/orbitron.html): kinetis/orbitron: a development-only construction harness — a portable Kinetis context document, the installed kinetis/* package inventory, a project-layout verification and one previewable health-endpoint scaffold, from a shell or over its own MCP server.
- [Agent Workflow](https://kinetis.dev/docs/agent-workflow.html): Entry point for an agent: the current-main/installed-version boundary, and where to route a task.
- [Application Recipes](https://kinetis.dev/docs/application-recipes.html): Routing recipes for common application tasks: the right pages, lifecycle/I-O boundary, security checks and verification for each.
- [Agent Correctness Review](https://kinetis.dev/docs/agent-correctness.html): A review checklist for persistent-worker, I/O, security and integrity correctness before calling a change done.

## Reference

- [Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/reference.html): Topic references for exact contracts, failure behavior and advanced wiring.
- [Appendix: Container Lifecycle](https://kinetis.dev/docs/container.html): AppScope, RequestScope, binding resolution and disposal.
- [Appendix: Configuration Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-configuration.html): Configuration resolution, scoped keys and the full key catalogue.
- [Appendix: Runtime](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-runtime.html): Request bodies, forwarded headers, adapters, Fibers and compiled artifacts.
- [Appendix: Testing](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-testing.html): Test-client request construction, loop liveness and runtime conformance.
- [Appendix: Observability](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-observability.html): Trace export, Fiber scope ownership and fingerprints.
- [Appendix: Routing and Validation](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-routing-validation.html): Route matching, request binding, validation and OpenAPI schema rules.
- [Appendix: Middleware](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-middleware.html): Pipeline order and built-in middleware contracts.
- [Appendix: Databases](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-database.html): Driver, transaction, pool and connection-registration contracts.
- [Appendix: Query Builder](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-query-builder.html): Advanced SQL composition and dialect behavior.
- [Appendix: Redis](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-redis.html): Redis transport, Cluster routing and cache mechanisms.
- [Appendix: Queue Contracts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-queue.html): Delivery semantics, worker lifecycle and backend mechanisms.
- [Appendix: Sessions Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-sessions.html): Cookie, CSRF, expiry and store lifecycle.
- [Appendix: Authentication Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-authentication.html): Bearer header grammar, JWT keys, validation and failure contracts.
- [Appendix: Storage Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-storage.html): Local publication, path confinement and S3 failure behavior.
- [Appendix: Search contracts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-search.html): Search configuration, client result and transport contracts.
- [Appendix: HTTP client contracts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-http-client.html): URL, header, deadline, response and transport contracts.
- [Appendix: AWS SigV4 contracts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-aws-sigv4.html): Signed-origin, credential, canonical request and failure contracts.
- [Appendix: MCP Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-mcp.html): Protocol, HTTP headers, errors and request lifecycle for application tools and resources.
- [Appendix: MCP Documentation Server Reference](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-mcp-docs.html): Installer, update, protocol and page-fetch contracts.
- [Appendix: System Layout](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix.html): A dense, file-by-file reference across every namespace in core.
- [Appendix: Satellite Packages](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-packages.html): A dense, file-by-file reference across every satellite package.
- [Appendix: Continuous Integration](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-ci.html): What CI actually tests, how, and what is deliberately not covered.
- [Appendix: Contributing to Kinetis](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-contributing.html): Contributing to Kinetis: the monorepo layout, dev environment setup, testing, the manifest-driven release tooling, and branching/PR/CI workflow.
